title: KfW 300: family home loan
description: A [subsidized loan program](rechner://law/kfw-300) for eligible families building or buying a qualifying climate-friendly home to live in.
benefit: A qualifying household can finance part of the project with a KfW loan; this is borrowing, not a grant.
limitation: Income, family, ownership and building requirements apply. An energy-efficiency expert must confirm the technical requirements.
calculatorEffect: The [Home Purchase Planner](rechner://app/housing) models a subset of eligibility conditions and caps the loan at the estimated financing need.

title: Owner-occupied EH 40 new build
description: Owner-occupied means you live in the home yourself. Efficiency House 40 (EH 40) is an energy-efficiency standard for a building.
benefit: The standard is one building requirement for the KfW 300 climate-friendly housing tiers.
limitation: KfW also requires lifecycle emissions limits, prohibits oil, gas or biomass heating, and requires expert confirmation. The first-purchase and household conditions also apply.
calculatorEffect: The switch is an assumption that the self-occupied home meets the program's building requirements; the calculator does not verify them.

title: QNG sustainability certification
description: The Quality Seal for Sustainable Buildings (Qualitätssiegel Nachhaltiges Gebäude, QNG) certifies sustainability. KfW 300 accepts the PLUS or PREMIUM tier for its higher funding level.
benefit: The QNG funding tier can allow a higher KfW loan ceiling.
limitation: A sustainability certificate, expert confirmation and the program's other building and household conditions are required.
calculatorEffect: The switch adds the configured QNG top-up to the potential loan ceiling, subject to modeled eligibility and financing need.

title: Taxable income (zvE)
description: Zu versteuerndes Einkommen (zvE) is the taxable income used as the basis for income tax after applicable adjustments and deductions; it is not the same as gross salary.
benefit: It provides the tax base for estimates and some income-dependent eligibility tests.
limitation: An estimate from salary inputs can differ from the amount on an official tax assessment. Programs may specify particular assessment years.
calculatorEffect: Enter the relevant taxable income for the modeled household or program rather than gross pay.

title: Joint assessment and splitting
description: Eligible spouses or registered partners can be assessed jointly. The splitting method calculates income tax using a shared tax base.
benefit: It can lower combined income tax compared with individual assessment, depending on each partner's income.
limitation: Eligibility and individual circumstances matter; payroll withholding classes do not themselves determine the final annual tax.
calculatorEffect: The joint setting applies the modeled splitting calculation to the estimate.

title: Payroll tax classes and ELStAM
description: A tax class is part of the electronic payroll tax information (ELStAM) used by an employer to withhold wage tax.
benefit: The class tailors withholding to the employee's registered circumstances.
limitation: Withholding is an advance, not necessarily the final annual income tax; changing class may also affect certain benefits.
calculatorEffect: The selected class changes modeled payroll withholding and, where relevant, the parental allowance estimate.

title: Parental allowance and parental leave
description: Elterngeld is an income-related family benefit; Elternzeit is leave from employment. They are related but separate arrangements.
benefit: Eligible parents can receive financial support while caring for a child; different allowance options can be combined under their rules.
limitation: Income, working hours, timing and other conditions affect eligibility and amounts. A simulation is not an official determination.
calculatorEffect: The planner estimates payments and cash flow from the entered household and leave timeline.

title: EU Blue Card
description: The [EU Blue Card](rechner://law/aufenthg-18g) is a residence permit for qualifying skilled employment, with requirements that depend on the applicant and job.
benefit: It provides a route to work and residence in Germany and may offer a route to settlement subject to additional conditions.
limitation: Recognition, occupation, salary and other requirements must be checked with the responsible authority; different thresholds can apply.
calculatorEffect: The [EU Blue Card & Visa Planner](rechner://app/visa) compares the supplied salary and occupation track with modeled thresholds; it does not decide permit eligibility.

title: Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte)
description: The Opportunity Card is a residence route for job seeking. Depending on qualifications, applicants may use a recognized qualification route or a points-based route.
benefit: It can provide time in Germany to seek qualifying employment when the requirements are met.
limitation: The points total is only part of the assessment; qualification, language, financial support and other requirements may apply.
calculatorEffect: The visa tool scores the entered factors and estimates stay costs; it does not verify documents or grant a permit.

title: Company car taxable benefit
description: Private use of an employer-provided car can be treated as a taxable non-cash benefit. Valuation can depend on the car and commuting method.
benefit: Eligible electric vehicles may use reduced valuation rates under applicable rules.
limitation: Actual payroll treatment depends on vehicle eligibility, use and the chosen valuation method; a taxable benefit is not the same as cash received.
calculatorEffect: The [Company Car Calculator](rechner://app/company-car) estimates the taxable amount and applies the entered marginal rate to approximate net cost.

title: Solar feed-in and tax treatment
description: A solar installation can supply household electricity and export surplus electricity to the grid. Feed-in compensation and tax treatment follow separate rules.
benefit: Self-consumption can reduce purchased electricity and eligible exported electricity can earn compensation.
limitation: Actual yield, tariffs, technical eligibility and tax treatment depend on the installation and commissioning details.
calculatorEffect: The [Solar Savings Calculator](rechner://app/solar-energy) uses entered yield, consumption and costs with modeled tariffs and assumptions; it is not a tax assessment.

title: Childcare costs and tax deduction
description: Qualifying childcare expenses can be considered as special expenses for income tax under the applicable conditions.
benefit: An eligible deduction can reduce taxable income and therefore the family's tax bill.
limitation: Not every expense qualifies: meals and the particular payment and documentation requirements must be considered. The deduction is not a euro-for-euro refund.
calculatorEffect: The Kita tool estimates eligible costs and their tax effect using the entered assumptions.

title: Minijob and Midijob
description: Minijob and Midijob are employment categories with different earnings limits and social-insurance treatment.
benefit: The transition-area rules can reduce an eligible employee's contribution burden; Minijobs have separate contribution and tax rules.
limitation: Classification, multiple jobs, pension-insurance choices and tax arrangements can change the result.
calculatorEffect: The tool estimates employee deductions using the selected pay, tax and insurance assumptions.

title: Commuting allowance and JobTicket
description: The distance allowance is a work-expense deduction for commuting. An employer-supported JobTicket has separate tax treatment that can affect the deduction.
benefit: Eligible work expenses may reduce taxable income; an eligible employer ticket can reduce the employee's travel cost.
limitation: The tax saving depends on the overall deduction and tax position. An employer subsidy must be taken into account; a deduction is not a refund of its full amount.
calculatorEffect: The tool compares modeled self-paid and employer-ticket scenarios using the entered costs and tax assumptions.

title: Qualification recognition
description: Recognition compares a foreign qualification with the relevant German qualification. A notice can identify substantial differences rather than full equivalence.
benefit: Recognition or partial recognition may support different skilled-worker or Opportunity Card routes.
limitation: The competent authority decides recognition. A degree, professional experience or a points estimate alone does not establish equivalence.
calculatorEffect: Choose the appropriate modeled recognition condition; the tool does not check the actual notice or qualification.

title: Zero VAT on eligible solar installations
description: A zero VAT rate can apply to qualifying supplies and installation of photovoltaic systems under the statutory conditions.
benefit: Eligible purchases are invoiced at a zero VAT rate.
limitation: The installation and supply must meet the statutory conditions; the setting is not a general exemption for every energy purchase.
calculatorEffect: The switch assumes the purchase qualifies when estimating system cost and payback.

title: Minijob pension insurance exemption
description: A Minijob employee can apply for exemption from compulsory pension insurance. The employer contribution and the employee's pension position are separate matters.
benefit: Exemption can increase current take-home pay by removing the modeled employee pension contribution.
limitation: Exemption affects compulsory pension-insurance coverage and entitlements; its consequences depend on the person's circumstances.
calculatorEffect: The switch removes the modeled employee pension contribution from the Minijob calculation.

title: Nursing-care insurance contributions
description: Social nursing-care insurance contributions depend on factors including parent status, children's ages and the place of employment.
benefit: Applicable child-related adjustments can reduce the employee contribution.
limitation: The qualifying details and evidence matter. Saxony has a different employee/employer allocation.
calculatorEffect: The calculator uses the entered parent and child details and Saxony setting to estimate the employee share.

title: Household craftsman tax credit
description: Certain labor costs for qualifying work in an existing household may qualify for an income-tax reduction.
benefit: An eligible credit reduces income tax subject to statutory limits.
limitation: Qualifying work, labor costs, invoices and payment rules matter. It is not a general subsidy for all new-build or material costs.
calculatorEffect: The home planner applies the modeled credit to the entered annual eligible labor cost; it does not verify the work or tax liability.

title: GiroCode and SEPA credit transfers
description: A GiroCode is a scannable payment symbol containing payment instructions in a format supported by participating banking apps. A SEPA credit transfer is a euro bank transfer under the SEPA scheme.
benefit: Scanning can fill the recipient and transfer details in a banking app, reducing manual typing.
limitation: The code does not send money or verify the recipient. Check the details in your banking app before approving a transfer; support varies by bank.
calculatorEffect: The generator creates a payment code locally from the entered transfer details. It does not submit the transfer.

title: Payment reference and purpose code
description: A remittance reference helps a recipient identify a payment. Structured references use a defined format; unstructured references contain free text. A purpose code describes the kind of payment.
benefit: An accurate reference can help the recipient match a transfer to an invoice or account.
limitation: Use the reference requested by the recipient; a purpose code is separate and optional. Bank support and format limits apply.
calculatorEffect: The generator places the selected reference format and optional purpose code into the payment code.

title: Solar system size and specific yield
description: Kilowatt-peak (kWp) describes a solar system's rated peak power under standard test conditions. Specific yield estimates annual electricity generation per kWp, in kWh per kWp per year.
benefit: Together they give a simple estimate of annual generation.
limitation: Actual output varies with location, shading, orientation, weather and system performance.
calculatorEffect: The estimate multiplies system size by specific yield; it is not a site survey.

title: Solar self-consumption and feed-in
description: Self-consumption is the share of generated electricity used by the household; feed-in is electricity exported to the grid.
benefit: Self-consumed electricity can replace grid purchases; eligible exports can earn compensation.
limitation: The actual share depends on when electricity is generated and used, batteries and other system details.
calculatorEffect: The entered share divides modeled generation between household use and exported electricity.

title: Gross list price for a company car
description: Bruttolistenpreis is the vehicle's gross domestic list price used as an input to the flat-rate valuation of private car use, rather than necessarily the amount paid for the car.
benefit: The list-price method offers a standardized way to estimate the taxable non-cash benefit.
limitation: Applicable rounding, eligible equipment, powertrain and valuation conditions matter.
calculatorEffect: The company-car tool applies modeled valuation percentages to the entered list price.

title: Company car commute valuation
description: A company car used for trips between home and the first workplace can generate an additional taxable benefit. The valuation can use a monthly method or a method based on actual trips, subject to the rules.
benefit: The available method can affect the amount added to taxable pay.
limitation: Actual use, employer payroll practice and documentation requirements matter.
calculatorEffect: Choose the modeled method and enter one-way distance and workplace days to compare the estimated amount.

title: Opportunity Card points factors
description: The points route considers qualifications, experience, language, age, previous stays and a qualifying partner. A shortage occupation is a profession in the applicable shortage list; partial recognition means an authority has identified differences from the German qualification. The prior-stay and partner factors have their own conditions.
benefit: Qualifying factors can contribute toward the points needed for the points-based route.
limitation: Each factor has its own conditions and evidence requirements; a calculated score alone does not establish eligibility.
calculatorEffect: The switches reflect factors assumed by this model and are not verification of the supporting documents.

title: Basiselterngeld and ElterngeldPlus
description: Basiselterngeld and ElterngeldPlus are different ways to receive parental allowance. ElterngeldPlus can spread an entitlement over a longer period and is often relevant when working part-time.
benefit: The options allow families to plan benefit timing around work and childcare.
limitation: Monthly amounts, claim periods and combinations depend on income, working time and the parents' situation.
calculatorEffect: The parental planner estimates monthly payments from the selected claim and work timeline.

title: Elterngeld partnership bonus
description: The partnership bonus provides additional ElterngeldPlus months when eligible parents share work and childcare and satisfy the applicable working-time conditions.
benefit: Qualifying parents can receive additional months of ElterngeldPlus.
limitation: Both parents must meet the relevant requirements over the claimed period; the exact rules depend on the family's circumstances.
calculatorEffect: The planner uses the entered work schedule to model the bonus, without verifying the official claim.

title: Elterngeld sibling bonus
description: The sibling bonus (Geschwisterbonus) is an addition to parental allowance for a qualifying family with older children.
benefit: It increases the allowance while the statutory conditions are satisfied.
limitation: The number and ages of the children and other eligibility conditions matter.
calculatorEffect: The planner uses the modeled family and birth timeline to estimate whether the bonus applies.

title: Maternity protection and pay
description: Mutterschutz is a legal protection period around childbirth; maternity benefits and employer payments can replace part of earnings during eligible periods.
benefit: It provides employment protection and, where eligible, financial support around birth.
limitation: Eligibility and payment sources depend on employment, insurance and individual circumstances; maternity benefits can affect parental allowance for the same period.
calculatorEffect: The parental planner estimates maternity cash flow and its interaction with modeled parental allowance.

title: Kindergeld and child tax allowances
description: Kindergeld is a child benefit. Child tax allowances are considered separately in the annual income-tax assessment.
benefit: Eligible families can receive child benefit and may receive additional tax relief when the statutory comparison is favorable.
limitation: The assessment coordinates child benefit and allowance relief; they are not simply two full independent payments.
calculatorEffect: The calculators use the modeled child count and assumptions; a complete individual eligibility assessment is not performed.

title: Payment code character encoding
description: Character encoding determines how text is represented in the payment symbol. UTF-8 supports a broad range of characters; the ASCII option converts text to a narrower character set.
benefit: The ASCII option can improve compatibility with systems that cannot handle all characters in the original text.
limitation: Conversion can change names and references. Verify the generated payment details and the recipient's requirements.
calculatorEffect: Choose whether the generator retains supported text as UTF-8 or uses its ASCII transliteration when building the payment code.

title: Mortgage financing and repayment
description: Mortgage interest is the cost of borrowing; initial repayment (Tilgung) is the part of the starting annual payment used to reduce the loan principal.
benefit: A higher repayment rate reduces the outstanding balance faster, all else being equal.
limitation: The interest rate, repayment schedule, fixed-rate period, fees and future refinancing can differ from this simple estimate.
calculatorEffect: The [Home Purchase Planner](rechner://app/housing) estimates the initial bank payment. The [Mortgage Simulator](rechner://app/mortgage) projects a balance using fixed rates; neither is a complete loan offer.

title: Purchase costs beyond the property price
description: The extra one-time costs of buying a home, such as property transfer tax, notary and land registry fees, and any buyer's estate-agent fee. These are in addition to the property's purchase price.
benefit: Including these costs helps you estimate the total cash needed to buy, instead of planning for the property price alone.
limitation: The amount depends on the property, location and transaction. An estimate is not a bill, and may not include every expense.
calculatorEffect: In the mortgage simulator this amount is used in the estimated purchase budget; changing it does not automatically change the separately entered bank loan. The Home Purchase Planner can calculate and transfer an estimate.

title: Bank loan amount
description: The amount you plan to borrow from a bank for the purchase. It is the starting balance you must repay, before any interest or payments.
benefit: Entering the amount makes it possible to estimate the bank payment, interest and remaining balance over time.
limitation: This amount excludes the separately entered KfW loan. The bank loan is borrowed money, not the price of the home or the combined total of all loans.
calculatorEffect: The mortgage simulator uses this value for the bank repayment and adds any KfW amount to total debt and loan-to-value. It is an independent input: changing the property price, savings or purchase costs here does not recalculate the loan amount. The Home Purchase Planner can calculate and transfer an estimate.

title: Loan-to-value (LTV)
description: Loan-to-value compares what you borrow with the value of the property. For example, €400,000 of loans divided by a €500,000 property value is 80%.
benefit: It helps you see how much of the property's value is covered by debt.
limitation: A lender can use its own property valuation and lending rules. Purchase costs financed by loans can make the ratio higher than 100%.
calculatorEffect: The simulator divides the starting bank loan plus the KfW loan by the property price or value you enter. Changing the value does not automatically change the loans.

title: Target bank payoff term
description: The payoff term is the time over which you want to repay the bank loan in full through regular monthly payments.
benefit: A longer term usually reduces the regular monthly payment; a shorter term generally means more principal is repaid sooner.
limitation: The payoff term is not necessarily the fixed-interest period. Actual rates can change when a fixed-rate period ends, and the lender's payment terms can differ.
calculatorEffect: In payoff-term mode the simulator estimates a fixed monthly bank payment that would repay the loan over the selected term, assuming the rate stays unchanged. Extra bank payments can shorten the payoff time.

title: Extra bank principal payment
description: An extra principal payment is money paid in addition to the regular bank installment to reduce the outstanding bank loan.
benefit: If permitted and paid consistently, it can reduce future interest and bring the bank payoff date forward.
limitation: Your agreement may restrict extra repayments or charge fees. This option does not pay down the separate KfW loan.
calculatorEffect: The simulator adds the entered amount to each bank payment until the bank loan is paid off and compares it with the same scenario without the extra payments.

title: KfW interest-only periods and lump sums
description: The nominal annual interest rate is the rate used to calculate interest; the effective rate can also reflect certain costs. The loan term is how long the loan runs. During an interest-only period you pay interest but do not reduce the loan balance. With a lump-sum loan, the borrowed principal is due at the end of its term.
benefit: An interest-only period can reduce the initial monthly payment, while repayment of the principal is postponed.
limitation: The debt remains outstanding during that period, and later payments or the final lump sum must still be paid. Available KfW terms depend on the offer and program.
calculatorEffect: Enter the terms from your offer. The simulator models either an initial interest-only period followed by monthly repayment, or interest-only payments followed by a lump sum; it does not check whether the chosen terms are offered.

title: Mortgage affordability estimate
description: An affordability estimate compares your household's income after tax with spending, home running costs and loan payments.
benefit: It shows the cash remaining each month under the amounts and loan terms you enter.
limitation: It is not a lender's approval or a guarantee. Costs, income, rates and KfW eligibility can change, and a future lump sum needs its own funding.
calculatorEffect: The simulator subtracts entered expenses, home costs and modeled loan payments. Its estimated purchase budget assumes fixed purchase costs, the entered KfW amount and all remaining cash are available; include any desired buffer in expenses.
